question_text: A physical quantity X depends on pressure P, volume V and time t as X = k P^a V^b t^c, where k is dimensionless. If X has the dimensions of angular momentum, which set of exponents is correct?
explanation: Pressure has dimensions [P] = M L^-1 T^-2, volume has [V] = L^3, and time has [t] = T. Thus [P^a V^b t^c] = M^a L^{-a+3b} T^{-2a+c}. Angular momentum has dimensions M L^2 T^-1. Equating powers gives a = 1, -a + 3b = 2, and -2a + c = -1. Substituting a = 1 gives -1 + 3b = 2, so b = 1, and -2 + c = -1, so c = 1. Hence the correct set is a = 1, b = 1, c = 1.

question_text: A quantity Q is proposed to depend on force F, density rho and speed v according to Q = C F^x rho^y v^z, where C is dimensionless. If Q has the dimensions of area, which of the following is correct?
explanation: The dimensions are [F] = M L T^-2, [rho] = M L^-3, and [v] = L T^-1. Therefore [F^x rho^y v^z] = M^{x+y} L^{x-3y+z} T^{-2x-z}. Since Q is an area, [Q] = L^2. Equating dimensions gives x + y = 0, x - 3y + z = 2, and -2x - z = 0. From -2x - z = 0, z = -2x. From x + y = 0, y = -x. Substituting into the length equation: x - 3(-x) - 2x = 2, so 2x = 2, hence x = 1. Therefore y = -1 and z = -2.
